title: Agricultural Processing Engineering
topics: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A container of volume 0.025 m3 holds 12 kg of maize when filled and struck off level. Calculate the bulk density of the maize in kg/m3.
items.s: Bulk density = mass/volume = 12/0.025 = 480 kg/m3.

items.q: A silo compartment holds 4 m3 of grain whose bulk density is 800 kg/m3. Calculate the mass of grain stored in tonnes.
items.s: Mass = bulk density x volume = 800 x 4 = 3200 kg = 3.2 tonnes.

items.q: A store must hold 1200 kg of grain whose bulk density is 600 kg/m3. Calculate the volume of storage space needed in m3.
items.s: Volume = mass/bulk density = 1200/600 = 2 m3.

items.q: A cleaner receives 200 kg of produce containing 40 kg of foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the percentage of foreign matter in the feed.
items.s: Foreign matter = 40/200 x 100 = 20 percent of the feed.

items.q: After grading, 450 kg of a 1000 kg lot falls into the first grade. Calculate the percentage of the lot in that grade.
items.s: Percentage in grade = grade mass/total mass x 100 = 450/1000 x 100 = 45 percent.

items.q: A milled lot of 600 kg contains 30 kg of broken grain. Calculate the percentage of broken grain.
items.s: Broken grain = 30/600 x 100 = 5 percent.

items.q: A hammer mill grinds 600 kg of maize in 6 hours. Calculate its capacity in kg/h.
items.s: Capacity = mass/time = 600/6 = 100 kg/h.

items.q: A thin layer of grain falls from 28 percent to 16 percent moisture content, wet basis, in 2 hours. Calculate the average drying rate in percentage points per hour.
items.s: Drying rate = fall in moisture/time = (28 - 16)/2 = 6 percentage points per hour.

items.q: A bulk of 5000 kg of maize suffers a storage loss of 3 percent over a season. Calculate the mass lost in kg.
items.s: Mass lost = stored mass x loss/100 = 5000 x 3/100 = 150 kg.

items.q: A sample of 500 g of seed is found to contain 220 g of oil. Calculate the oil content in percent.
items.s: Oil content = oil/seed x 100 = 220/500 x 100 = 44 percent.

items.q: A press is fed 1200 kg of copra of 24 percent oil content and all the oil is removed. Calculate the mass of cake left in kg.
items.s: Cake = seed x (100 - oil content)/100 = 1200 x 76/100 = 912 kg.

items.q: An expeller presses 600 kg of seed in 2 hours. Calculate its pressing rate in kg/h.
items.s: Pressing rate = mass/time = 600/2 = 300 kg/h.

items.q: A lot of 750 kg of nuts has a kernel content of 68 percent. Calculate the mass of kernel expected in kg.
items.s: Kernel mass = nut mass x kernel content/100 = 750 x 68/100 = 510 kg.

items.q: A sheller handles 2000 kg of maize in 3 hours. Calculate its throughput in kg/h.
items.s: Throughput = mass/time = 2000/3 = 666.7 kg/h.

items.q: A sheller cracks 90 kg out of 1000 kg of kernel handled. Calculate the percentage breakage.
items.s: Breakage = cracked kernel/total kernel x 100 = 90/1000 x 100 = 9 percent.

items.q: A belt conveyor runs at 1 m/s and carries 30 kg of material on each metre of its length. Calculate its capacity in kg/s.
items.s: Capacity = belt speed x load per metre = 1 x 30 = 30 kg/s.

items.q: A conveyor moves 18 tonnes of produce per hour. Calculate the mass moved in 6 hours in tonnes.
items.s: Mass moved = rate x time = 18 x 6 = 108 tonnes.

items.q: A plant processes 1200 kg of raw material and obtains 650 kg of product. Calculate the processing yield in percent.
items.s: Processing yield = product/raw material x 100 = 650/1200 x 100 = 54.2 percent.

items.q: A grain sample weighs 299 g when taken and 185 g after all its moisture has been driven off. Calculate its moisture content on the dry basis in percent.
items.s: Dry basis moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/dry mass x 100 = (299 - 185)/185 x 100 = 61.62 percent.

items.q: A crop has a moisture content of 16 percent on the wet basis. Calculate the same moisture on the dry basis in percent.
items.s: Dry basis = wet basis/(100 - wet basis) x 100 = 16/(100 - 16) x 100 = 19.05 percent.

items.q: A heap of grain has a bulk density of 720 kg/m3 while the true density of the kernels is 1350 kg/m3. Calculate the porosity of the bulk in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/true density) x 100 = (1 - 720/1350) x 100 = 46.7 percent.

items.q: A grain particle released into still air falls 1.2 m at a steady speed in 1.2 s. Calculate its terminal velocity in m/s.
items.s: Terminal velocity = distance/time = 1.2/1.2 = 1 m/s.

items.q: A lot of 1500 kg of grain has a moisture content of 16 percent on the wet basis. Calculate the mass of water it contains in kg.
items.s: Mass of water = total mass x moisture/100 = 1500 x 16/100 = 240 kg.

items.q: A cleaner is fed 500 kg of paddy that contains 8 percent foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the mass of cleaned paddy obtained in kg.
items.s: Clean paddy = feed x (100 - foreign matter)/100 = 500 x 92/100 = 460 kg.

items.q: Of 75 kg of material small enough to pass a screen, only 70 kg actually passes. Calculate the screen efficiency in percent.
items.s: Screen efficiency = mass passed/mass that should pass x 100 = 70/75 x 100 = 93.3 percent.

items.q: A lot of 800 kg of produce is found to contain 3 percent foreign matter, all of which must be removed. Calculate the mass rejected in kg.
items.s: Rejected mass = feed x foreign matter/100 = 800 x 3/100 = 24 kg.

items.q: A mill takes in material of average particle size 18 mm and turns out a product of average size 0.5 mm. Calculate the size reduction ratio.
items.s: Reduction ratio = feed size/product size = 18/0.5 = 36.

items.q: A mill of 11 kW runs for 1.5 hours to grind 2000 kg of grain. Calculate the specific energy used in kWh per tonne.
items.s: Energy used = 11 x 1.5 = 16.5 kWh, so specific energy = 16.5/2 tonnes = 8.25 kWh per tonne.

items.q: A miller grinds 2000 kg of wheat and obtains 1400 kg of flour. Calculate the extraction rate in percent.
items.s: Extraction rate = flour/grain x 100 = 1400/2000 x 100 = 70 percent.

items.q: A screen must handle 1200 kg/h of material and the permissible loading is 200 kg per hour per square metre of screen. Calculate the screen area required in m2.
items.s: Screen area = throughput/loading = 1200/200 = 6 m2.

items.q: A lot of 2500 kg of grain is to be dried from 24 percent to 13 percent moisture content, both on the wet basis. Calculate the mass of water to be removed in kg.
items.s: Water removed = mass x (initial - final)/(100 - final) = 2500 x (24 - 13)/(87) = 316.1 kg.

items.q: A lot of 2500 kg of paddy at 20 percent moisture is dried to 12 percent, both on the wet basis. Calculate the final mass in kg.
items.s: Final mass = initial mass x (100 - initial moisture)/(100 - final moisture) = 2500 x 80/88 = 2273 kg.

items.q: A dryer removes 40 kg of water from 500 kg of grain and the latent heat of vaporisation is taken as 2600 kJ/kg. Calculate the heat needed for evaporation in MJ.
items.s: Heat = water removed x latent heat = 40 x 2600 kJ = 104000 kJ = 104 MJ.

items.q: A dryer is supplied with 220 MJ of heat and uses 110 MJ in evaporating water from the grain. Calculate its thermal efficiency in percent.
items.s: Thermal efficiency = heat used/heat supplied x 100 = 110/220 x 100 = 50 percent.

items.q: A fan delivers 6000 m3/h of air through a bulk of 15 tonnes of grain. Calculate the airflow rate in m3 per hour per tonne.
items.s: Airflow rate = volume of air/mass = 6000/15 = 400 m3 per hour per tonne.

items.q: A lot of 1200 kg of grain at 26 percent moisture is held in air that brings it into equilibrium at 15 percent moisture, wet basis. Calculate the mass of the grain at equilibrium in kg.
items.s: Equilibrium mass = initial mass x (100 - initial moisture)/(100 - equilibrium moisture) = 1200 x 74/85 = 1045 kg.

items.q: A store holds 5 tonnes of grain and the bulk loses 25 kg each day to insects and spillage. Calculate the number of days before 5 percent of the bulk has been lost.
items.s: Mass to be lost = 5 x 1000 x 5/100 = 250 kg, so days = 250/25 = 10 days.

items.q: Airflow of 600 m3 per minute is passed through a bulk of grain and the air rises 10 degrees in temperature, its specific heat being taken as 0.6 kJ per m3 per degree. Calculate the heat carried away per minute in kJ.
items.s: Heat carried away = airflow x temperature rise x specific heat = 600 x 10 x 0.6 = 3600 kJ per minute.

items.q: A bulk of 25 tonnes of grain is to be cooled with air supplied at 0.5 m3 per second per tonne. Calculate the total airflow required in m3 per second.
items.s: Total airflow = mass x airflow rate = 25 x 0.5 = 50 m3 per second.

items.q: A cylindrical silo is 5 m in diameter and 10 m tall and is filled to 0.8 of its height. Calculate the volume of grain it holds in m3.
items.s: Volume = (pi/4) x diameter^2 x filled height = (pi/4) x 5^2 x 10 x 0.8 = 157.1 m3.

items.q: A silo holds 220 m3 of maize whose bulk density is 780 kg/m3. Calculate the mass of maize in tonnes.
items.s: Mass = volume x bulk density = 220 x 780 = 171600 kg = 171.6 tonnes.

items.q: A press is fed 800 kg of groundnut seed of 22 percent oil content and recovers 85 percent of the oil present. Calculate the mass of oil obtained in kg.
items.s: Oil in the seed = 800 x 22/100 = 176 kg, so oil recovered = 176 x 85/100 = 149.6 kg.

items.q: A solvent plant recovers 210 kg of oil from seed that contains 300 kg of oil. Calculate the extraction efficiency in percent.
items.s: Extraction efficiency = oil recovered/oil in seed x 100 = 210/300 x 100 = 70 percent.

items.q: A sheller receives 1000 kg of groundnut in shell and delivers 680 kg of shelled kernel. Calculate the shelling efficiency in percent.
items.s: Shelling efficiency = kernel obtained/in shell fed x 100 = 680/1000 x 100 = 68 percent.

items.q: A thresher delivers 1200 kg of grain and leaves 45 kg of unthreshed grain in the straw. Calculate the threshing loss as a percentage of the total grain.
items.s: Threshing loss = grain lost/(grain delivered + grain lost) x 100 = 45/1245 x 100 = 3.61 percent.

items.q: A bucket elevator lifts 30 tonnes of grain per hour through a height of 12 m. Taking g as 9.81 m/s2, calculate the power needed to raise the material in kW.
items.s: Power = mass rate x g x height = 30 x 1000/3600 x 9.81 x 12 = 0.98 kW.

items.q: A screw conveyor of 0.15 m diameter and 0.2 m pitch turns at 50 revolutions per minute, is 0.45 full and handles material of bulk density 750 kg/m3. Calculate its capacity in kg/s.
items.s: Capacity = (pi/4) d^2 x pitch x fill x speed x density = (pi/4) x 0.15^2 x 0.2 x 0.45 x 0.8333 x 750 = 0.99 kg/s.

items.q: A conveyor must move material over a distance of 90 m at a belt speed of 1.5 m/s. Calculate the time the material spends on the belt in seconds.
items.s: Time = distance/speed = 90/1.5 = 60 seconds.

items.q: Calculate the heat needed to raise 200 kg of water through 40 degrees, taking the specific heat of water as 4.186 kJ/kg per degree. Give the answer in MJ.
items.s: Heat = mass x specific heat x rise = 200 x 4.186 x 40 = 33488 kJ = 33.49 MJ.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: Calculate the heat needed to turn 20 kg of saturated water at its boiling point into dry saturated steam, the latent heat being 2300 kJ/kg. Give the answer in MJ.
items.s: Heat = mass x latent heat = 20 x 2300 = 46000 kJ = 46 MJ.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A boiler takes in fuel giving 2000 MJ of heat and passes 1800 MJ into the steam it raises. Calculate the boiler efficiency in percent.
items.s: Boiler efficiency = heat in steam/heat in fuel x 100 = 1800/2000 x 100 = 90 percent.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A process needs 4800 MJ of heat, the fuel burned has a calorific value of 38 MJ/kg and the furnace efficiency is 75 percent. Calculate the mass of fuel required in kg.
items.s: Useful heat per kg = 38 x 75/100 = 28.5 MJ, so fuel = 4800/28.5 = 168.4 kg.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A flat wall of thickness 0.08 m and area 2 m2 has a thermal conductivity of 0.25 W/m per degree. If the faces differ in temperature by 20 degrees, calculate the heat flow through the wall in W.
items.s: Heat flow = k A dT/thickness = 0.25 x 2 x 20/0.08 = 125 W.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A processing unit of 3 kW runs for 2 hours and turns out 600 kg of product. Calculate the specific energy consumption in kWh per tonne.
items.s: Energy = 3 x 2 = 6 kWh and mass = 0.6 tonnes, so specific energy = 6/0.6 = 10 kWh per tonne.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A plant has an annual fixed cost of 120000 naira, a variable cost of 400 naira per tonne processed, and handles 1200 tonnes in the year. Calculate the unit processing cost in naira per tonne.
items.s: Total cost = 120000 + 400 x 1200 = 600000 naira, so unit cost = 600000/1200 = 500 naira per tonne.

items.q: A processing plant was designed to handle 4000 tonnes a season but actually handled 2100 tonnes. Calculate its capacity utilisation in percent.
items.s: Capacity utilisation = actual/design x 100 = 2100/4000 x 100 = 52.5 percent.

items.q: A plant processes 2500 kg of raw material and turns out 12 percent of it as a saleable by product worth 60 naira per kg. Calculate the value of the by product in naira.
items.s: By product mass = 2500 x 12/100 = 300 kg, so value = 300 x 60 = 18000 naira.

items.q: A process receives 1500 kg of raw material, turns out 600 kg of main product and rejects 120 kg as waste. Calculate the mass unaccounted for, taken as material lost in the plant, in kg.
items.s: Loss = feed - product - waste = 1500 - 600 - 120 = 780 kg.

items.q: A sample of paddy has a mass of 194 g before drying and 183 g after oven drying. Calculate its moisture content on the wet basis in percent.
items.s: Wet basis moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/wet mass x 100 = (194 - 183)/194 x 100 = 5.67 percent.

items.q: A container of volume 0.04 m3 holds 18 kg of maize when filled and struck off level. Calculate the bulk density of the maize in kg/m3.
items.s: Bulk density = mass/volume = 18/0.04 = 450 kg/m3.

items.q: sensible heat may be defined as
o: the sorting of produce into lots of uniform size, shape or quality
the stage of drying in which the surface begins to dry and the rate of evaporation slows
heat that changes the temperature of a substance without changing its state
the solid residue left after oil has been pressed from seed
items.s: sensible heat: heat that changes the temperature of a substance without changing its state. The other options describe falling rate period, grading, cake.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: throughput may be defined as
o: a conveyor in which an endless moving band carries the material
the mass of produce a machine handles in unit time
a tall cylindrical structure for holding grain in bulk
the perforated plate that holds material in the grinding zone until it is fine enough to pass
items.s: throughput: the mass of produce a machine handles in unit time. The other options describe belt conveyor, silo, screen in a mill.

items.q: angle of repose may be defined as
o: a conveyor in which cups fixed to a vertical belt or chain lift material upward
a device in which heat passes from a hot fluid to a cold one without the two mixing
the turning of process residues into useful material instead of discarding them
the steepest angle to the horizontal that a heap of the material will stand at without sliding
items.s: angle of repose: the steepest angle to the horizontal that a heap of the material will stand at without sliding. The other options describe heat exchanger, waste recovery, bucket elevator.

items.q: Which term is described by “the solid residue left after oil has been pressed from seed”?
o: refining
extraction efficiency
expeller
cake
items.s: cake is the solid residue left after oil has been pressed from seed.

items.q: The statement “an acid formed when a fat splits, used as a measure of the quality of an oil” describes which of the following?
o: refining
free fatty acid
expeller
solvent extraction
items.s: free fatty acid is an acid formed when a fat splits, used as a measure of the quality of an oil.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines free fatty acid?
o: the forcing of air through a bulk of stored produce to cool it or to level its moisture
the stage of drying in which the surface begins to dry and the rate of evaporation slows
an acid formed when a fat splits, used as a measure of the quality of an oil
the heat needed to raise the temperature of unit mass of a substance by one degree
items.s: free fatty acid: an acid formed when a fat splits, used as a measure of the quality of an oil. The other options describe specific heat, falling rate period, aeration.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines thin layer drying?
o: an acid formed when a fat splits, used as a measure of the quality of an oil
the drying of a sample shallow enough that the air conditions are the same throughout it
injury to the living embryo of a seed caused by rough handling or overheating
the steepest angle to the horizontal that a heap of the material will stand at without sliding
items.s: thin layer drying: the drying of a sample shallow enough that the air conditions are the same throughout it. The other options describe germination damage, angle of repose, free fatty acid.

items.q: Which term is described by “material of low thermal conductivity wrapped round a vessel to slow the loss of heat”?
o: steam quality
thermal conductivity
boiler efficiency
insulation
items.s: insulation is material of low thermal conductivity wrapped round a vessel to slow the loss of heat.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: Which term is described by “the stage of drying in which the surface begins to dry and the rate of evaporation slows”?
o: falling rate period
equilibrium moisture content
drying rate
bound moisture
items.s: falling rate period is the stage of drying in which the surface begins to dry and the rate of evaporation slows.

items.q: Which of the following best describes fixed cost?
o: injury to the living embryo of a seed caused by rough handling or overheating
the fall in quantity or quality of produce that takes place while it is held in store
an expense of the plant that does not change with the quantity processed
the fraction by mass of a steam sample that is vapour rather than suspended droplets
items.s: fixed cost: an expense of the plant that does not change with the quantity processed. The other options describe steam quality, germination damage, storage losses.

items.q: unit processing cost may be defined as
o: the total cost of a process divided by the mass of product turned out
water held in a material in excess of the amount that balances the surrounding air
an acid formed when a fat splits, used as a measure of the quality of an oil
the fall in quantity or quality of produce that takes place while it is held in store
items.s: unit processing cost: the total cost of a process divided by the mass of product turned out. The other options describe storage losses, free fatty acid, free moisture.

items.q: The statement “the share of the heat released by the fuel that is taken up by the water and steam” describes which of the following?
o: heat exchanger
boiler efficiency
thermal conductivity
specific heat
items.s: boiler efficiency is the share of the heat released by the fuel that is taken up by the water and steam.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: The statement “the sorting of particles by the density difference between them” describes which of the following?
o: foreign matter
magnetic separator
specific gravity separation
sieving
items.s: specific gravity separation is the sorting of particles by the density difference between them.

items.q: Which term is described by “the lifting away of light impurities from a falling stream of produce by suction”?
o: screen efficiency
foreign matter
sieving
aspiration
items.s: aspiration is the lifting away of light impurities from a falling stream of produce by suction.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines magnetic separator?
o: a device that removes pieces of iron from a stream of produce as it passes
the mass of water in a material expressed as a percentage of the total mass of the wet material
the removal of the hard outer covering from a nut or grain
a machine that moves material continuously between two points along a fixed path
items.s: magnetic separator: a device that removes pieces of iron from a stream of produce as it passes. The other options describe shelling, moisture content wet basis, conveyor.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines threshing?
o: a device in which heat passes from a hot fluid to a cold one without the two mixing
a mill in which free swinging hammers beat the material against a screen
the mass of a material divided by the volume of its solid matter alone, with all pores excluded
the loosening of grain from the ear by beating or rubbing
items.s: threshing: the loosening of grain from the ear by beating or rubbing. The other options describe hammer mill, true density, heat exchanger.

items.q: The statement “the volume of air passed through a bulk of produce for each unit of its mass in unit time” describes which of the following?
o: airflow rate
hermetic storage
fumigation
chilling injury
items.s: airflow rate is the volume of air passed through a bulk of produce for each unit of its mass in unit time.

items.q: Which term is described by “a secondary material of value obtained alongside the main product of a process”?
o: by product
material balance
waste recovery
processing yield
items.s: by product is a secondary material of value obtained alongside the main product of a process.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines conveyor.
o: a machine that moves material continuously between two points along a fixed path
a conveyor in which cups fixed to a vertical belt or chain lift material upward
the proportion of the seed present in a lot that is successfully freed from its shell
the keeping of produce in a sealed container in which the air is not renewed
items.s: conveyor: a machine that moves material continuously between two points along a fixed path. The other options describe shelling efficiency, bucket elevator, hermetic storage.

items.q: The statement “damage to produce caused by holding it below the temperature it can tolerate” describes which of the following?
o: aeration
chilling injury
storage losses
mould spoilage
items.s: chilling injury is damage to produce caused by holding it below the temperature it can tolerate.

items.q: Which of the following best describes heat exchanger?
o: the steepest slope at which a belt conveyor can carry a given material without it rolling back
a conveyor in which a turning helical flight pushes material along a trough
the proportion of oil held in a seed on a stated basis
a device in which heat passes from a hot fluid to a cold one without the two mixing
items.s: heat exchanger: a device in which heat passes from a hot fluid to a cold one without the two mixing. The other options describe oil content, inclination limit, screw conveyor.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: foreign matter may be defined as
o: the mass of water in a material expressed as a percentage of the mass of its dry matter
material present in a produce lot other than the produce itself
the share of the material that should pass a screen which actually does pass it
the pressing of oil out of prepared seed by mechanical force
items.s: foreign matter: material present in a produce lot other than the produce itself. The other options describe screen efficiency, expression, moisture content dry basis.

items.q: insulation may be defined as
o: a mill that crushes grain between pairs of smooth or fluted rollers
an expense that rises in step with the quantity of material processed
material of low thermal conductivity wrapped round a vessel to slow the loss of heat
the stage of drying in which water evaporates from the surface as fast as it arrives there
items.s: insulation: material of low thermal conductivity wrapped round a vessel to slow the loss of heat. The other options describe constant rate period, roller mill, variable cost.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: The statement “the angle the surface of material heaped on a moving belt makes with the horizontal” describes which of the following?
o: belt conveyor
inclination limit
surcharge angle
bucket elevator
items.s: surcharge angle is the angle the surface of material heaped on a moving belt makes with the horizontal.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines true density.
o: the loosening of grain from the ear by beating or rubbing
a substance that takes up or gives off moisture until it is in balance with the surrounding air
the mass of a material divided by the volume of its solid matter alone, with all pores excluded
material present in a produce lot other than the produce itself
items.s: true density: the mass of a material divided by the volume of its solid matter alone, with all pores excluded. The other options describe threshing, hygroscopic material, foreign matter.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines by product?
o: the mass of oil recovered from a stated mass of seed
a secondary material of value obtained alongside the main product of a process
the separation of particles by passing them through openings of a chosen size
the angle the surface of material heaped on a moving belt makes with the horizontal
items.s: by product: a secondary material of value obtained alongside the main product of a process. The other options describe oil yield, sieving, surcharge angle.

items.q: Which term is described by “the mass of a wanted component recovered as a fraction of the mass of raw material fed”?
o: material balance
by product
variable cost
extraction rate
items.s: extraction rate is the mass of a wanted component recovered as a fraction of the mass of raw material fed.

items.q: Which of the following best describes sphericity?
o: the share of the material that should pass a screen which actually does pass it
the mass of a material divided by the volume of its solid matter alone, with all pores excluded
water held in a material in excess of the amount that balances the surrounding air
a measure of how closely the shape of a particle approaches a sphere
items.s: sphericity: a measure of how closely the shape of a particle approaches a sphere. The other options describe free moisture, true density, screen efficiency.

items.q: All of the following belong to Process economics and product yield EXCEPT
o: material balance
aspiration
extraction rate
processing yield
items.s: Every other option belongs to Process economics and product yield. “aspiration” belongs to Cleaning, grading and sorting, not Process economics and product yield.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines evaporation?
o: the size of the feed divided by the size of the product of a mill
the perforated plate that holds material in the grinding zone until it is fine enough to pass
the change of water into vapour at a temperature below its boiling point
the steepest angle to the horizontal that a heap of the material will stand at without sliding
items.s: evaporation: the change of water into vapour at a temperature below its boiling point. The other options describe angle of repose, screen in a mill, size reduction ratio.

items.q: expeller may be defined as
o: a screw press that squeezes oil from seed and pushes out a pressed cake
an index of how easily a material can be ground to a stated fineness
injury to the living embryo of a seed caused by rough handling or overheating
the turning of process residues into useful material instead of discarding them
items.s: expeller: a screw press that squeezes oil from seed and pushes out a pressed cake. The other options describe waste recovery, germination damage, hardgrove grindability.

items.q: magnetic separator may be defined as
o: material present in a produce lot other than the produce itself
a device that removes pieces of iron from a stream of produce as it passes
the separation of chaff from grain by a stream of air
the sorting of produce into lots of uniform size, shape or quality
items.s: magnetic separator: a device that removes pieces of iron from a stream of produce as it passes. The other options describe grading, foreign matter, winnowing.

items.q: The statement “the keeping of produce in a sealed container in which the air is not renewed” describes which of the following?
o: hot spot
silo
hermetic storage
storage losses
items.s: hermetic storage is the keeping of produce in a sealed container in which the air is not renewed.

items.q: The statement “the heat liberated when unit mass of a fuel is completely burned” describes which of the following?
o: sensible heat
thermal conductivity
calorific value
latent heat of vaporisation
items.s: calorific value is the heat liberated when unit mass of a fuel is completely burned.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: Which statement correctly defines deep bed drying?
o: the stage of drying in which water evaporates from the surface as fast as it arrives there
the drying of a layer of grain so thick that the air changes conditions as it passes through
the mass of water in a material expressed as a percentage of the mass of its dry matter
the loosening of grain from the ear by beating or rubbing
items.s: deep bed drying: the drying of a layer of grain so thick that the air changes conditions as it passes through. The other options describe threshing, constant rate period, moisture content dry basis.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines deep bed drying.
o: the total cost of a process divided by the mass of product turned out
the drying of a layer of grain so thick that the air changes conditions as it passes through
the fall in quantity or quality of produce that takes place while it is held in store
the share of the oil present in the seed that the process actually recovers
items.s: deep bed drying: the drying of a layer of grain so thick that the air changes conditions as it passes through. The other options describe extraction efficiency, unit processing cost, storage losses.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines specific gravity separation.
o: the sorting of particles by the density difference between them
a substance that takes up or gives off moisture until it is in balance with the surrounding air
the removal of the hard outer covering from a nut or grain
the lifting away of light impurities from a falling stream of produce by suction
items.s: specific gravity separation: the sorting of particles by the density difference between them. The other options describe hygroscopic material, shelling, aspiration.

items.q: Which term is described by “the mass of oil recovered from a stated mass of seed”?
o: expeller
oil content
oil yield
cake
items.s: oil yield is the mass of oil recovered from a stated mass of seed.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines conveyor capacity.
o: the mass or volume of material a conveyor moves in unit time
the stage of drying in which water evaporates from the surface as fast as it arrives there
material of low thermal conductivity wrapped round a vessel to slow the loss of heat

a mill that breaks material by rubbing it between two surfaces

injury to the living embryo of a seed caused by rough handling or overheating

belt conveyor
pneumatic conveyor

items.q: A heap of grain has a bulk density of 680 kg/m3 while the true density of the kernels is 1350 kg/m3. Calculate the porosity of the bulk in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/true density) x 100 = (1 - 680/1350) x 100 = 49.6 percent.

items.q: A lot of 800 kg of grain has a moisture content of 20 percent on the wet basis. Calculate the mass of water it contains in kg.
items.s: Mass of water = total mass x moisture/100 = 800 x 20/100 = 160 kg.

items.q: A cleaner is fed 500 kg of paddy that contains 10 percent foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the mass of cleaned paddy obtained in kg.
items.s: Clean paddy = feed x (100 - foreign matter)/100 = 500 x 90/100 = 450 kg.

items.q: A lot of 600 kg of produce is found to contain 6 percent foreign matter, all of which must be removed. Calculate the mass rejected in kg.
items.s: Rejected mass = feed x foreign matter/100 = 600 x 6/100 = 36 kg.

items.q: A mill takes in material of average particle size 20 mm and turns out a product of average size 0.75 mm. Calculate the size reduction ratio.
items.s: Reduction ratio = feed size/product size = 20/0.75 = 26.67.

items.q: A miller grinds 1000 kg of wheat and obtains 700 kg of flour. Calculate the extraction rate in percent.
items.s: Extraction rate = flour/grain x 100 = 700/1000 x 100 = 70 percent.

items.q: A lot of 2000 kg of paddy at 22 percent moisture is dried to 13 percent, both on the wet basis. Calculate the final mass in kg.
items.s: Final mass = initial mass x (100 - initial moisture)/(100 - final moisture) = 2000 x 78/87 = 1793 kg.

items.q: A dryer removes 85 kg of water from 1500 kg of grain and the latent heat of vaporisation is taken as 2600 kJ/kg. Calculate the heat needed for evaporation in MJ.
items.s: Heat = water removed x latent heat = 85 x 2600 kJ = 221000 kJ = 221 MJ.

items.q: A dryer is supplied with 260 MJ of heat and uses 70 MJ in evaporating water from the grain. Calculate its thermal efficiency in percent.
items.s: Thermal efficiency = heat used/heat supplied x 100 = 70/260 x 100 = 26.9 percent.

items.q: A store holds 15 tonnes of grain and the bulk loses 15 kg each day to insects and spillage. Calculate the number of days before 4 percent of the bulk has been lost.
items.s: Mass to be lost = 15 x 1000 x 4/100 = 600 kg, so days = 600/15 = 40 days.

items.q: A bulk of 15 tonnes of grain is to be cooled with air supplied at 2 m3 per second per tonne. Calculate the total airflow required in m3 per second.
items.s: Total airflow = mass x airflow rate = 15 x 2 = 7.5 m3 per second.

items.q: A silo holds 220 m3 of maize whose bulk density is 750 kg/m3. Calculate the mass of maize in tonnes.
items.s: Mass = volume x bulk density = 220 x 750 = 165000 kg = 165 tonnes.

items.q: A solvent plant recovers 180 kg of oil from seed that contains 250 kg of oil. Calculate the extraction efficiency in percent.
items.s: Extraction efficiency = oil recovered/oil in seed x 100 = 180/250 x 100 = 72 percent.

items.q: A sheller receives 800 kg of groundnut in shell and delivers 740 kg of shelled kernel. Calculate the shelling efficiency in percent.
items.s: Shelling efficiency = kernel obtained/in shell fed x 100 = 740/800 x 100 = 92.5 percent.

items.q: A conveyor must move material over a distance of 45 m at a belt speed of 0.75 m/s. Calculate the time the material spends on the belt in seconds.
items.s: Time = distance/speed = 45/0.75 = 60 seconds.

items.q: Calculate the heat needed to raise 50 kg of water through 40 degrees, taking the specific heat of water as 4.186 kJ/kg per degree. Give the answer in MJ.
items.s: Heat = mass x specific heat x rise = 50 x 4.186 x 40 = 8372 kJ = 8.37 MJ.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: Calculate the heat needed to turn 20 kg of saturated water at its boiling point into dry saturated steam, the latent heat being 2257 kJ/kg. Give the answer in MJ.
items.s: Heat = mass x latent heat = 20 x 2257 = 45140 kJ = 45.1 MJ.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A processing unit of 5.5 kW runs for 2 hours and turns out 400 kg of product. Calculate the specific energy consumption in kWh per tonne.
items.s: Energy = 5.5 x 2 = 11 kWh and mass = 0.4 tonnes, so specific energy = 11/0.4 = 27.5 kWh per tonne.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A processing plant was designed to handle 5000 tonnes a season but actually handled 1400 tonnes. Calculate its capacity utilisation in percent.
items.s: Capacity utilisation = actual/design x 100 = 1400/5000 x 100 = 28 percent.

items.q: A process receives 2500 kg of raw material, turns out 600 kg of main product and rejects 50 kg as waste. Calculate the mass unaccounted for, taken as material lost in the plant, in kg.
items.s: Loss = feed - product - waste = 2500 - 600 - 50 = 1850 kg.

items.q: A sample of paddy has a mass of 205 g before drying and 160 g after oven drying. Calculate its moisture content on the wet basis in percent.
items.s: Wet basis moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/wet mass x 100 = (205 - 160)/205 x 100 = 21.95 percent.

items.q: A crop has a moisture content of 22 percent on the wet basis. Calculate the same moisture on the dry basis in percent.
items.s: Dry basis = wet basis/(100 - wet basis) x 100 = 22/(100 - 22) x 100 = 28.21 percent.

items.q: A silo compartment holds 2 m3 of grain whose bulk density is 750 kg/m3. Calculate the mass of grain stored in tonnes.
items.s: Mass = bulk density x volume = 750 x 2 = 1500 kg = 1.5 tonnes.

items.q: A grain particle released into still air falls 1.2 m at a steady speed in 1 s. Calculate its terminal velocity in m/s.
items.s: Terminal velocity = distance/time = 1.2/1 = 1.2 m/s.

items.q: A store must hold 1200 kg of grain whose bulk density is 700 kg/m3. Calculate the volume of storage space needed in m3.
items.s: Volume = mass/bulk density = 1200/700 = 1.71 m3.

items.q: A cleaner receives 200 kg of produce containing 50 kg of foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the percentage of foreign matter in the feed.
items.s: Foreign matter = 50/200 x 100 = 25 percent of the feed.

items.q: Of 60 kg of material small enough to pass a screen, only 52 kg actually passes. Calculate the screen efficiency in percent.
items.s: Screen efficiency = mass passed/mass that should pass x 100 = 52/60 x 100 = 86.7 percent.

items.q: After grading, 900 kg of a 1500 kg lot falls into the first grade. Calculate the percentage of the lot in that grade.
items.s: Percentage in grade = grade mass/total mass x 100 = 900/1500 x 100 = 60 percent.

items.q: A hammer mill grinds 1500 kg of maize in 4 hours. Calculate its capacity in kg/h.
items.s: Capacity = mass/time = 1500/4 = 375 kg/h.

items.q: A mill of 15 kW runs for 2.5 hours to grind 1500 kg of grain. Calculate the specific energy used in kWh per tonne.
items.s: Energy used = 15 x 2.5 = 37.5 kWh, so specific energy = 37.5/1.5 tonnes = 25 kWh per tonne.

items.q: A screen must handle 1600 kg/h of material and the permissible loading is 300 kg per hour per square metre of screen. Calculate the screen area required in m2.
items.s: Screen area = throughput/loading = 1600/300 = 5.33 m2.

items.q: A lot of 1000 kg of grain is to be dried from 26 percent to 14 percent moisture content, both on the wet basis. Calculate the mass of water to be removed in kg.
items.s: Water removed = mass x (initial - final)/(100 - final) = 1000 x (26 - 14)/(86) = 139.5 kg.

items.q: A thin layer of grain falls from 28 percent to 16 percent moisture content, wet basis, in 5 hours. Calculate the average drying rate in percentage points per hour.
items.s: Drying rate = fall in moisture/time = (28 - 16)/5 = 2.4 percentage points per hour.

items.q: A fan delivers 4800 m3/h of air through a bulk of 10 tonnes of grain. Calculate the airflow rate in m3 per hour per tonne.
items.s: Airflow rate = volume of air/mass = 4800/10 = 480 m3 per hour per tonne.

items.q: A lot of 1200 kg of grain at 24 percent moisture is held in air that brings it into equilibrium at 15 percent moisture, wet basis. Calculate the mass of the grain at equilibrium in kg.
items.s: Equilibrium mass = initial mass x (100 - initial moisture)/(100 - equilibrium moisture) = 1200 x 76/85 = 1073 kg.

items.q: A bulk of 3000 kg of maize suffers a storage loss of 4 percent over a season. Calculate the mass lost in kg.
items.s: Mass lost = stored mass x loss/100 = 3000 x 4/100 = 120 kg.

items.q: Airflow of 1200 m3 per minute is passed through a bulk of grain and the air rises 6 degrees in temperature, its specific heat being taken as 0.8 kJ per m3 per degree. Calculate the heat carried away per minute in kJ.
items.s: Heat carried away = airflow x temperature rise x specific heat = 1200 x 6 x 0.8 = 5760 kJ per minute.

items.q: A cylindrical silo is 4.5 m in diameter and 12 m tall and is filled to 0.8 of its height. Calculate the volume of grain it holds in m3.
items.s: Volume = (pi/4) x diameter^2 x filled height = (pi/4) x 4.5^2 x 12 x 0.8 = 152.7 m3.

items.q: A press is fed 800 kg of groundnut seed of 28 percent oil content and recovers 80 percent of the oil present. Calculate the mass of oil obtained in kg.
items.s: Oil in the seed = 800 x 28/100 = 224 kg, so oil recovered = 224 x 80/100 = 179.2 kg.

items.q: A sample of 1250 g of seed is found to contain 220 g of oil. Calculate the oil content in percent.
items.s: Oil content = oil/seed x 100 = 220/1250 x 100 = 17.6 percent.

items.q: A press is fed 1200 kg of copra of 22 percent oil content and all the oil is removed. Calculate the mass of cake left in kg.
items.s: Cake = seed x (100 - oil content)/100 = 1200 x 78/100 = 936 kg.

items.q: An expeller presses 1200 kg of seed in 5 hours. Calculate its pressing rate in kg/h.
items.s: Pressing rate = mass/time = 1200/5 = 240 kg/h.

items.q: A lot of 600 kg of nuts has a kernel content of 65 percent. Calculate the mass of kernel expected in kg.
items.s: Kernel mass = nut mass x kernel content/100 = 600 x 65/100 = 390 kg.

items.q: A thresher delivers 1200 kg of grain and leaves 60 kg of unthreshed grain in the straw. Calculate the threshing loss as a percentage of the total grain.
items.s: Threshing loss = grain lost/(grain delivered + grain lost) x 100 = 60/1260 x 100 = 4.76 percent.

items.q: A sheller handles 2500 kg of maize in 4 hours. Calculate its throughput in kg/h.
items.s: Throughput = mass/time = 2500/4 = 625 kg/h.

items.q: A sheller cracks 25 kg out of 1000 kg of kernel handled. Calculate the percentage breakage.
items.s: Breakage = cracked kernel/total kernel x 100 = 25/1000 x 100 = 2.5 percent.

items.q: A belt conveyor runs at 1.2 m/s and carries 30 kg of material on each metre of its length. Calculate its capacity in kg/s.
items.s: Capacity = belt speed x load per metre = 1.2 x 30 = 36 kg/s.

items.q: A conveyor moves 45 tonnes of produce per hour. Calculate the mass moved in 4 hours in tonnes.
items.s: Mass moved = rate x time = 45 x 4 = 180 tonnes.

items.q: A bucket elevator lifts 40 tonnes of grain per hour through a height of 8 m. Taking g as 9.81 m/s2, calculate the power needed to raise the material in kW.
items.s: Power = mass rate x g x height = 40 x 1000/3600 x 9.81 x 8 = 0.87 kW.

items.q: A screw conveyor of 0.2 m diameter and 0.25 m pitch turns at 50 revolutions per minute, is 0.4 full and handles material of bulk density 750 kg/m3. Calculate its capacity in kg/s.
items.s: Capacity = (pi/4) d^2 x pitch x fill x speed x density = (pi/4) x 0.2^2 x 0.25 x 0.4 x 0.8333 x 750 = 1.96 kg/s.

items.q: A boiler takes in fuel giving 4000 MJ of heat and passes 3000 MJ into the steam it raises. Calculate the boiler efficiency in percent.
items.s: Boiler efficiency = heat in steam/heat in fuel x 100 = 3000/4000 x 100 = 75 percent.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A process needs 4800 MJ of heat, the fuel burned has a calorific value of 44 MJ/kg and the furnace efficiency is 65 percent. Calculate the mass of fuel required in kg.
items.s: Useful heat per kg = 44 x 65/100 = 28.6 MJ, so fuel = 4800/28.6 = 167.8 kg.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A flat wall of thickness 0.05 m and area 4 m2 has a thermal conductivity of 0.4 W/m per degree. If the faces differ in temperature by 40 degrees, calculate the heat flow through the wall in W.
items.s: Heat flow = k A dT/thickness = 0.4 x 4 x 40/0.05 = 1280 W.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A plant processes 1200 kg of raw material and obtains 975 kg of product. Calculate the processing yield in percent.
items.s: Processing yield = product/raw material x 100 = 975/1200 x 100 = 81.2 percent.

items.q: A plant has an annual fixed cost of 300000 naira, a variable cost of 320 naira per tonne processed, and handles 800 tonnes in the year. Calculate the unit processing cost in naira per tonne.
items.s: Total cost = 300000 + 320 x 800 = 556000 naira, so unit cost = 556000/800 = 695 naira per tonne.

items.q: A plant processes 2500 kg of raw material and turns out 15 percent of it as a saleable by product worth 60 naira per kg. Calculate the value of the by product in naira.
items.s: By product mass = 2500 x 15/100 = 375 kg, so value = 375 x 60 = 22500 naira.

items.q: A grain sample weighs 257 g when taken and 147 g after all its moisture has been driven off. Calculate its moisture content on the dry basis in percent.
items.s: Dry basis moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/dry mass x 100 = (257 - 147)/147 x 100 = 74.83 percent.

items.q: A heap of grain has a bulk density of 780 kg/m3 while the true density of the kernels is 1350 kg/m3. Calculate the porosity of the bulk in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/true density) x 100 = (1 - 780/1350) x 100 = 42.2 percent.

items.q: A lot of 2000 kg of grain has a moisture content of 20 percent on the wet basis. Calculate the mass of water it contains in kg.
items.s: Mass of water = total mass x moisture/100 = 2000 x 20/100 = 400 kg.

items.q: A cleaner is fed 600 kg of paddy that contains 6 percent foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the mass of cleaned paddy obtained in kg.
items.s: Clean paddy = feed x (100 - foreign matter)/100 = 600 x 94/100 = 564 kg.

a conveyor in which material is carried along a pipe by a stream of air
the mass or volume of material a conveyor moves in unit time
a conveyor in which an endless moving band carries the material

the solid residue left after oil has been pressed from seed
the proportion of oil held in a seed on a stated basis
a screw press that squeezes oil from seed and pushes out a pressed cake

items.q: chilling injury is best described as

refining
oil content
solvent extraction

size reduction ratio
attrition mill
hardgrove grindability

items.q: A grain particle released into still air falls 1 m at a steady speed in 1.5 s. Calculate its terminal velocity in m/s.
items.s: Terminal velocity = distance/time = 1/1.5 = 0.667 m/s.

items.q: Of 90 kg of material small enough to pass a screen, only 45 kg actually passes. Calculate the screen efficiency in percent.
items.s: Screen efficiency = mass passed/mass that should pass x 100 = 45/90 x 100 = 50 percent.

items.q: A mill of 11 kW runs for 3 hours to grind 1500 kg of grain. Calculate the specific energy used in kWh per tonne.
items.s: Energy used = 11 x 3 = 33 kWh, so specific energy = 33/1.5 tonnes = 22 kWh per tonne.

items.q: A lot of 2000 kg of grain is to be dried from 26 percent to 13 percent moisture content, both on the wet basis. Calculate the mass of water to be removed in kg.
items.s: Water removed = mass x (initial - final)/(100 - final) = 2000 x (26 - 13)/(87) = 298.9 kg.

items.q: A fan delivers 2400 m3/h of air through a bulk of 8 tonnes of grain. Calculate the airflow rate in m3 per hour per tonne.
items.s: Airflow rate = volume of air/mass = 2400/8 = 300 m3 per hour per tonne.

items.q: Airflow of 1000 m3 per minute is passed through a bulk of grain and the air rises 6 degrees in temperature, its specific heat being taken as 0.7 kJ per m3 per degree. Calculate the heat carried away per minute in kJ.
items.s: Heat carried away = airflow x temperature rise x specific heat = 1000 x 6 x 0.7 = 4200 kJ per minute.

items.q: A cylindrical silo is 3.5 m in diameter and 15 m tall and is filled to 0.8 of its height. Calculate the volume of grain it holds in m3.
items.s: Volume = (pi/4) x diameter^2 x filled height = (pi/4) x 3.5^2 x 15 x 0.8 = 115.5 m3.

items.q: A press is fed 800 kg of groundnut seed of 20 percent oil content and recovers 90 percent of the oil present. Calculate the mass of oil obtained in kg.
items.s: Oil in the seed = 800 x 20/100 = 160 kg, so oil recovered = 160 x 90/100 = 144 kg.

items.q: A thresher delivers 1800 kg of grain and leaves 45 kg of unthreshed grain in the straw. Calculate the threshing loss as a percentage of the total grain.
items.s: Threshing loss = grain lost/(grain delivered + grain lost) x 100 = 45/1845 x 100 = 2.44 percent.

items.q: A bucket elevator lifts 30 tonnes of grain per hour through a height of 15 m. Taking g as 9.81 m/s2, calculate the power needed to raise the material in kW.
items.s: Power = mass rate x g x height = 30 x 1000/3600 x 9.81 x 15 = 1.23 kW.

items.q: A boiler takes in fuel giving 3600 MJ of heat and passes 3000 MJ into the steam it raises. Calculate the boiler efficiency in percent.
items.s: Boiler efficiency = heat in steam/heat in fuel x 100 = 3000/3600 x 100 = 83.3 percent.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A flat wall of thickness 0.05 m and area 4 m2 has a thermal conductivity of 0.15 W/m per degree. If the faces differ in temperature by 40 degrees, calculate the heat flow through the wall in W.
items.s: Heat flow = k A dT/thickness = 0.15 x 4 x 40/0.05 = 480 W.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A plant has an annual fixed cost of 120000 naira, a variable cost of 480 naira per tonne processed, and handles 1500 tonnes in the year. Calculate the unit processing cost in naira per tonne.
items.s: Total cost = 120000 + 480 x 1500 = 840000 naira, so unit cost = 840000/1500 = 560 naira per tonne.

items.q: A plant processes 1500 kg of raw material and turns out 20 percent of it as a saleable by product worth 50 naira per kg. Calculate the value of the by product in naira.
items.s: By product mass = 1500 x 20/100 = 300 kg, so value = 300 x 50 = 15000 naira.

items.q: A sample of paddy has a mass of 304 g before drying and 144 g after oven drying. Calculate its moisture content on the wet basis in percent.
items.s: Wet basis moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/wet mass x 100 = (304 - 144)/304 x 100 = 52.63 percent.

items.q: A grain sample weighs 259 g when taken and 200 g after all its moisture has been driven off. Calculate its moisture content on the dry basis in percent.
items.s: Dry basis moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/dry mass x 100 = (259 - 200)/200 x 100 = 29.5 percent.

items.q: A container of volume 0.02 m3 holds 12 kg of maize when filled and struck off level. Calculate the bulk density of the maize in kg/m3.
items.s: Bulk density = mass/volume = 12/0.02 = 600 kg/m3.

items.q: A heap of grain has a bulk density of 700 kg/m3 while the true density of the kernels is 1350 kg/m3. Calculate the porosity of the bulk in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/true density) x 100 = (1 - 700/1350) x 100 = 48.1 percent.

items.q: A silo compartment holds 5 m3 of grain whose bulk density is 650 kg/m3. Calculate the mass of grain stored in tonnes.
items.s: Mass = bulk density x volume = 650 x 5 = 3250 kg = 3.25 tonnes.

items.q: A store must hold 900 kg of grain whose bulk density is 800 kg/m3. Calculate the volume of storage space needed in m3.
items.s: Volume = mass/bulk density = 900/800 = 1.12 m3.

items.q: A lot of 1000 kg of grain has a moisture content of 16 percent on the wet basis. Calculate the mass of water it contains in kg.
items.s: Mass of water = total mass x moisture/100 = 1000 x 16/100 = 160 kg.

items.q: A cleaner receives 500 kg of produce containing 40 kg of foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the percentage of foreign matter in the feed.
items.s: Foreign matter = 40/500 x 100 = 8 percent of the feed.

items.q: A cleaner is fed 500 kg of paddy that contains 4 percent foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the mass of cleaned paddy obtained in kg.
items.s: Clean paddy = feed x (100 - foreign matter)/100 = 500 x 96/100 = 480 kg.

items.q: After grading, 750 kg of a 1000 kg lot falls into the first grade. Calculate the percentage of the lot in that grade.
items.s: Percentage in grade = grade mass/total mass x 100 = 750/1000 x 100 = 75 percent.

items.q: A lot of 1000 kg of produce is found to contain 5 percent foreign matter, all of which must be removed. Calculate the mass rejected in kg.
items.s: Rejected mass = feed x foreign matter/100 = 1000 x 5/100 = 50 kg.

items.q: A milled lot of 600 kg contains 45 kg of broken grain. Calculate the percentage of broken grain.
items.s: Broken grain = 45/600 x 100 = 7.5 percent.

items.q: A mill takes in material of average particle size 12 mm and turns out a product of average size 0.4 mm. Calculate the size reduction ratio.
items.s: Reduction ratio = feed size/product size = 12/0.4 = 30.

items.q: A hammer mill grinds 1800 kg of maize in 2 hours. Calculate its capacity in kg/h.
items.s: Capacity = mass/time = 1800/2 = 900 kg/h.

items.q: A miller grinds 2000 kg of wheat and obtains 1050 kg of flour. Calculate the extraction rate in percent.
items.s: Extraction rate = flour/grain x 100 = 1050/2000 x 100 = 52.5 percent.

items.q: A lot of 1500 kg of paddy at 20 percent moisture is dried to 12 percent, both on the wet basis. Calculate the final mass in kg.
items.s: Final mass = initial mass x (100 - initial moisture)/(100 - final moisture) = 1500 x 80/88 = 1364 kg.

items.q: A dryer removes 70 kg of water from 1500 kg of grain and the latent heat of vaporisation is taken as 2400 kJ/kg. Calculate the heat needed for evaporation in MJ.
items.s: Heat = water removed x latent heat = 70 x 2400 kJ = 168000 kJ = 168 MJ.

items.q: A thin layer of grain falls from 26 percent to 16 percent moisture content, wet basis, in 3 hours. Calculate the average drying rate in percentage points per hour.
items.s: Drying rate = fall in moisture/time = (26 - 16)/3 = 3.33 percentage points per hour.

items.q: A dryer is supplied with 180 MJ of heat and uses 140 MJ in evaporating water from the grain. Calculate its thermal efficiency in percent.
items.s: Thermal efficiency = heat used/heat supplied x 100 = 140/180 x 100 = 77.8 percent.

items.q: A lot of 1500 kg of grain at 28 percent moisture is held in air that brings it into equilibrium at 14 percent moisture, wet basis. Calculate the mass of the grain at equilibrium in kg.
items.s: Equilibrium mass = initial mass x (100 - initial moisture)/(100 - equilibrium moisture) = 1500 x 72/86 = 1256 kg.

items.q: A bulk of 8000 kg of maize suffers a storage loss of 4 percent over a season. Calculate the mass lost in kg.
items.s: Mass lost = stored mass x loss/100 = 8000 x 4/100 = 320 kg.

items.q: A store holds 15 tonnes of grain and the bulk loses 20 kg each day to insects and spillage. Calculate the number of days before 5 percent of the bulk has been lost.
items.s: Mass to be lost = 15 x 1000 x 5/100 = 750 kg, so days = 750/20 = 37.5 days.

items.q: A bulk of 25 tonnes of grain is to be cooled with air supplied at 1 m3 per second per tonne. Calculate the total airflow required in m3 per second.
items.s: Total airflow = mass x airflow rate = 25 x 1 = 25 m3 per second.

items.q: A silo holds 260 m3 of maize whose bulk density is 780 kg/m3. Calculate the mass of maize in tonnes.
items.s: Mass = volume x bulk density = 260 x 780 = 202800 kg = 202.8 tonnes.

items.q: A sample of 1500 g of seed is found to contain 170 g of oil. Calculate the oil content in percent.
items.s: Oil content = oil/seed x 100 = 170/1500 x 100 = 11.3 percent.

items.q: A solvent plant recovers 230 kg of oil from seed that contains 250 kg of oil. Calculate the extraction efficiency in percent.
items.s: Extraction efficiency = oil recovered/oil in seed x 100 = 230/250 x 100 = 92 percent.

items.q: A press is fed 1000 kg of copra of 20 percent oil content and all the oil is removed. Calculate the mass of cake left in kg.
items.s: Cake = seed x (100 - oil content)/100 = 1000 x 80/100 = 800 kg.

items.q: An expeller presses 1000 kg of seed in 4 hours. Calculate its pressing rate in kg/h.
items.s: Pressing rate = mass/time = 1000/4 = 250 kg/h.

items.q: A sheller receives 800 kg of groundnut in shell and delivers 330 kg of shelled kernel. Calculate the shelling efficiency in percent.
items.s: Shelling efficiency = kernel obtained/in shell fed x 100 = 330/800 x 100 = 41.2 percent.

items.q: A lot of 600 kg of nuts has a kernel content of 68 percent. Calculate the mass of kernel expected in kg.
items.s: Kernel mass = nut mass x kernel content/100 = 600 x 68/100 = 408 kg.

items.q: A sheller handles 1600 kg of maize in 2 hours. Calculate its throughput in kg/h.
items.s: Throughput = mass/time = 1600/2 = 800 kg/h.

items.q: A sheller cracks 90 kg out of 1200 kg of kernel handled. Calculate the percentage breakage.
items.s: Breakage = cracked kernel/total kernel x 100 = 90/1200 x 100 = 7.5 percent.

items.q: A belt conveyor runs at 2 m/s and carries 18 kg of material on each metre of its length. Calculate its capacity in kg/s.
items.s: Capacity = belt speed x load per metre = 2 x 18 = 36 kg/s.

items.q: A conveyor moves 12 tonnes of produce per hour. Calculate the mass moved in 4 hours in tonnes.
items.s: Mass moved = rate x time = 12 x 4 = 48 tonnes.

items.q: A screw conveyor of 0.25 m diameter and 0.15 m pitch turns at 40 revolutions per minute, is 0.45 full and handles material of bulk density 750 kg/m3. Calculate its capacity in kg/s.
items.s: Capacity = (pi/4) d^2 x pitch x fill x speed x density = (pi/4) x 0.25^2 x 0.15 x 0.45 x 0.6667 x 750 = 1.66 kg/s.

items.q: A conveyor must move material over a distance of 30 m at a belt speed of 1.5 m/s. Calculate the time the material spends on the belt in seconds.
items.s: Time = distance/speed = 30/1.5 = 20 seconds.

items.q: Calculate the heat needed to raise 150 kg of water through 20 degrees, taking the specific heat of water as 4.186 kJ/kg per degree. Give the answer in MJ.
items.s: Heat = mass x specific heat x rise = 150 x 4.186 x 20 = 12558 kJ = 12.56 MJ.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: Calculate the heat needed to turn 75 kg of saturated water at its boiling point into dry saturated steam, the latent heat being 2100 kJ/kg. Give the answer in MJ.
items.s: Heat = mass x latent heat = 75 x 2100 = 157500 kJ = 157.5 MJ.

items.q: A process needs 6000 MJ of heat, the fuel burned has a calorific value of 44 MJ/kg and the furnace efficiency is 65 percent. Calculate the mass of fuel required in kg.

items.q: A processing unit of 5.5 kW runs for 3 hours and turns out 600 kg of product. Calculate the specific energy consumption in kWh per tonne.

items.q: A plant processes 1500 kg of raw material and obtains 780 kg of product. Calculate the processing yield in percent.
items.s: Processing yield = product/raw material x 100 = 780/1500 x 100 = 52 percent.

items.q: A processing plant was designed to handle 2000 tonnes a season but actually handled 2100 tonnes. Calculate its capacity utilisation in percent.
items.s: Capacity utilisation = actual/design x 100 = 2100/2000 x 100 = 105 percent.

items.q: A process receives 2500 kg of raw material, turns out 1500 kg of main product and rejects 80 kg as waste. Calculate the mass unaccounted for, taken as material lost in the plant, in kg.
items.s: Loss = feed - product - waste = 2500 - 1500 - 80 = 920 kg.

items.q: A grain particle released into still air falls 1.5 m at a steady speed in 0.6 s. Calculate its terminal velocity in m/s.
items.s: Terminal velocity = distance/time = 1.5/0.6 = 2.5 m/s.

items.q: Of 40 kg of material small enough to pass a screen, only 35 kg actually passes. Calculate the screen efficiency in percent.

items.q: A screw conveyor of 0.2 m diameter and 0.12 m pitch turns at 75 revolutions per minute, is 0.4 full and handles material of bulk density 700 kg/m3. Calculate its capacity in kg/s.
items.s: Capacity = (pi/4) d^2 x pitch x fill x speed x density = (pi/4) x 0.2^2 x 0.12 x 0.4 x 1.25 x 700 = 1.32 kg/s.

items.q: A process needs 2400 MJ of heat, the fuel burned has a calorific value of 42 MJ/kg and the furnace efficiency is 70 percent. Calculate the mass of fuel required in kg.
items.s: Useful heat per kg = 42 x 70/100 = 29.4 MJ, so fuel = 2400/29.4 = 81.6 kg.

items.q: A sample of paddy has a mass of 182 g before drying and 175 g after oven drying. Calculate its moisture content on the wet basis in percent.
items.s: Wet basis moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/wet mass x 100 = (182 - 175)/182 x 100 = 3.85 percent.

items.q: A grain sample weighs 208 g when taken and 128 g after all its moisture has been driven off. Calculate its moisture content on the dry basis in percent.
items.s: Dry basis moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/dry mass x 100 = (208 - 128)/128 x 100 = 62.5 percent.

items.q: A crop has a moisture content of 14 percent on the wet basis. Calculate the same moisture on the dry basis in percent.
items.s: Dry basis = wet basis/(100 - wet basis) x 100 = 14/(100 - 14) x 100 = 16.28 percent.

items.q: A container of volume 0.04 m3 holds 22 kg of maize when filled and struck off level. Calculate the bulk density of the maize in kg/m3.
items.s: Bulk density = mass/volume = 22/0.04 = 550 kg/m3.

items.q: A heap of grain has a bulk density of 780 kg/m3 while the true density of the kernels is 1150 kg/m3. Calculate the porosity of the bulk in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/true density) x 100 = (1 - 780/1150) x 100 = 32.2 percent.

items.q: A silo compartment holds 2 m3 of grain whose bulk density is 600 kg/m3. Calculate the mass of grain stored in tonnes.
items.s: Mass = bulk density x volume = 600 x 2 = 1200 kg = 1.2 tonnes.

items.q: A store must hold 1500 kg of grain whose bulk density is 750 kg/m3. Calculate the volume of storage space needed in m3.
items.s: Volume = mass/bulk density = 1500/750 = 2 m3.

items.q: A lot of 1000 kg of grain has a moisture content of 14 percent on the wet basis. Calculate the mass of water it contains in kg.
items.s: Mass of water = total mass x moisture/100 = 1000 x 14/100 = 140 kg.

items.q: A cleaner receives 250 kg of produce containing 25 kg of foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the percentage of foreign matter in the feed.
items.s: Foreign matter = 25/250 x 100 = 10 percent of the feed.

items.q: A cleaner is fed 500 kg of paddy that contains 6 percent foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the mass of cleaned paddy obtained in kg.
items.s: Clean paddy = feed x (100 - foreign matter)/100 = 500 x 94/100 = 470 kg.

items.q: Of 75 kg of material small enough to pass a screen, only 45 kg actually passes. Calculate the screen efficiency in percent.
items.s: Screen efficiency = mass passed/mass that should pass x 100 = 45/75 x 100 = 60 percent.

items.q: After grading, 900 kg of a 800 kg lot falls into the first grade. Calculate the percentage of the lot in that grade.
items.s: Percentage in grade = grade mass/total mass x 100 = 900/800 x 100 = 112.5 percent.

items.q: A milled lot of 1000 kg contains 24 kg of broken grain. Calculate the percentage of broken grain.
items.s: Broken grain = 24/1000 x 100 = 2.4 percent.

items.q: A hammer mill grinds 1500 kg of maize in 5 hours. Calculate its capacity in kg/h.
items.s: Capacity = mass/time = 1500/5 = 300 kg/h.

items.q: A miller grinds 1500 kg of wheat and obtains 700 kg of flour. Calculate the extraction rate in percent.
items.s: Extraction rate = flour/grain x 100 = 700/1500 x 100 = 46.7 percent.

items.q: A lot of 3000 kg of grain is to be dried from 26 percent to 15 percent moisture content, both on the wet basis. Calculate the mass of water to be removed in kg.
items.s: Water removed = mass x (initial - final)/(100 - final) = 3000 x (26 - 15)/(85) = 388.2 kg.

items.q: A lot of 2000 kg of paddy at 20 percent moisture is dried to 12 percent, both on the wet basis. Calculate the final mass in kg.
items.s: Final mass = initial mass x (100 - initial moisture)/(100 - final moisture) = 2000 x 80/88 = 1818 kg.

items.q: A dryer removes 100 kg of water from 1200 kg of grain and the latent heat of vaporisation is taken as 2600 kJ/kg. Calculate the heat needed for evaporation in MJ.
items.s: Heat = water removed x latent heat = 100 x 2600 kJ = 260000 kJ = 260 MJ.

items.q: A dryer is supplied with 150 MJ of heat and uses 140 MJ in evaporating water from the grain. Calculate its thermal efficiency in percent.
items.s: Thermal efficiency = heat used/heat supplied x 100 = 140/150 x 100 = 93.3 percent.

items.q: A fan delivers 6000 m3/h of air through a bulk of 6 tonnes of grain. Calculate the airflow rate in m3 per hour per tonne.
items.s: Airflow rate = volume of air/mass = 6000/6 = 1000 m3 per hour per tonne.

items.q: A bulk of 4000 kg of maize suffers a storage loss of 3 percent over a season. Calculate the mass lost in kg.
items.s: Mass lost = stored mass x loss/100 = 4000 x 3/100 = 120 kg.

items.q: A store holds 8 tonnes of grain and the bulk loses 20 kg each day to insects and spillage. Calculate the number of days before 5 percent of the bulk has been lost.
items.s: Mass to be lost = 8 x 1000 x 5/100 = 400 kg, so days = 400/20 = 20 days.

items.q: Airflow of 800 m3 per minute is passed through a bulk of grain and the air rises 10 degrees in temperature, its specific heat being taken as 1 kJ per m3 per degree. Calculate the heat carried away per minute in kJ.
items.s: Heat carried away = airflow x temperature rise x specific heat = 800 x 10 x 1 = 8000 kJ per minute.

items.q: A bulk of 10 tonnes of grain is to be cooled with air supplied at 0.5 m3 per second per tonne. Calculate the total airflow required in m3 per second.
items.s: Total airflow = mass x airflow rate = 10 x 0.5 = 20 m3 per second.

items.q: A cylindrical silo is 4.5 m in diameter and 15 m tall and is filled to 0.8 of its height. Calculate the volume of grain it holds in m3.
items.s: Volume = (pi/4) x diameter^2 x filled height = (pi/4) x 4.5^2 x 15 x 0.8 = 190.9 m3.

items.q: A silo holds 120 m3 of maize whose bulk density is 780 kg/m3. Calculate the mass of maize in tonnes.
items.s: Mass = volume x bulk density = 120 x 780 = 93600 kg = 93.6 tonnes.

items.q: A press is fed 1200 kg of groundnut seed of 18 percent oil content and recovers 90 percent of the oil present. Calculate the mass of oil obtained in kg.
items.s: Oil in the seed = 1200 x 18/100 = 216 kg, so oil recovered = 216 x 90/100 = 194.4 kg.

items.q: An expeller presses 800 kg of seed in 4 hours. Calculate its pressing rate in kg/h.
items.s: Pressing rate = mass/time = 800/4 = 200 kg/h.

items.q: A sheller receives 600 kg of groundnut in shell and delivers 330 kg of shelled kernel. Calculate the shelling efficiency in percent.
items.s: Shelling efficiency = kernel obtained/in shell fed x 100 = 330/600 x 100 = 55 percent.

items.q: A lot of 900 kg of nuts has a kernel content of 75 percent. Calculate the mass of kernel expected in kg.
items.s: Kernel mass = nut mass x kernel content/100 = 900 x 75/100 = 675 kg.

items.q: A thresher delivers 2500 kg of grain and leaves 90 kg of unthreshed grain in the straw. Calculate the threshing loss as a percentage of the total grain.
items.s: Threshing loss = grain lost/(grain delivered + grain lost) x 100 = 90/2590 x 100 = 3.47 percent.

items.q: A sheller handles 2500 kg of maize in 3 hours. Calculate its throughput in kg/h.
items.s: Throughput = mass/time = 2500/3 = 833.3 kg/h.

items.q: A sheller cracks 75 kg out of 1500 kg of kernel handled. Calculate the percentage breakage.
items.s: Breakage = cracked kernel/total kernel x 100 = 75/1500 x 100 = 5 percent.

items.q: A belt conveyor runs at 1 m/s and carries 50 kg of material on each metre of its length. Calculate its capacity in kg/s.
items.s: Capacity = belt speed x load per metre = 1 x 50 = 50 kg/s.

items.q: A bucket elevator lifts 40 tonnes of grain per hour through a height of 10 m. Taking g as 9.81 m/s2, calculate the power needed to raise the material in kW.
items.s: Power = mass rate x g x height = 40 x 1000/3600 x 9.81 x 10 = 1.09 kW.

items.q: A conveyor must move material over a distance of 120 m at a belt speed of 1 m/s. Calculate the time the material spends on the belt in seconds.
items.s: Time = distance/speed = 120/1 = 120 seconds.

items.q: Calculate the heat needed to raise 150 kg of water through 50 degrees, taking the specific heat of water as 4.186 kJ/kg per degree. Give the answer in MJ.
items.s: Heat = mass x specific heat x rise = 150 x 4.186 x 50 = 31395 kJ = 31.39 MJ.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A flat wall of thickness 0.05 m and area 5 m2 has a thermal conductivity of 0.25 W/m per degree. If the faces differ in temperature by 40 degrees, calculate the heat flow through the wall in W.
items.s: Heat flow = k A dT/thickness = 0.25 x 5 x 40/0.05 = 1000 W.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A processing unit of 11 kW runs for 5 hours and turns out 400 kg of product. Calculate the specific energy consumption in kWh per tonne.
items.s: Energy = 11 x 5 = 55 kWh and mass = 0.4 tonnes, so specific energy = 55/0.4 = 137.5 kWh per tonne.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A plant processes 2000 kg of raw material and obtains 1300 kg of product. Calculate the processing yield in percent.
items.s: Processing yield = product/raw material x 100 = 1300/2000 x 100 = 65 percent.

items.q: A plant has an annual fixed cost of 300000 naira, a variable cost of 400 naira per tonne processed, and handles 1500 tonnes in the year. Calculate the unit processing cost in naira per tonne.
items.s: Total cost = 300000 + 400 x 1500 = 900000 naira, so unit cost = 900000/1500 = 600 naira per tonne.

items.q: A processing plant was designed to handle 2000 tonnes a season but actually handled 1800 tonnes. Calculate its capacity utilisation in percent.
items.s: Capacity utilisation = actual/design x 100 = 1800/2000 x 100 = 90 percent.

items.q: A plant processes 1500 kg of raw material and turns out 15 percent of it as a saleable by product worth 40 naira per kg. Calculate the value of the by product in naira.
items.s: By product mass = 1500 x 15/100 = 225 kg, so value = 225 x 40 = 9000 naira.

items.q: A process receives 1000 kg of raw material, turns out 1500 kg of main product and rejects 50 kg as waste. Calculate the mass unaccounted for, taken as material lost in the plant, in kg.
items.s: Loss = feed - product - waste = 1000 - 1500 - 50 = -550 kg.

items.q: A lot of 800 kg of grain at 26 percent moisture is held in air that brings it into equilibrium at 13 percent moisture, wet basis. Calculate the mass of the grain at equilibrium in kg.
items.s: Equilibrium mass = initial mass x (100 - initial moisture)/(100 - equilibrium moisture) = 800 x 74/87 = 680.5 kg.

items.q: A screw conveyor of 0.3 m diameter and 0.12 m pitch turns at 50 revolutions per minute, is 0.5 full and handles material of bulk density 750 kg/m3. Calculate its capacity in kg/s.
items.s: Capacity = (pi/4) d^2 x pitch x fill x speed x density = (pi/4) x 0.3^2 x 0.12 x 0.5 x 0.8333 x 750 = 2.65 kg/s.

items.q: A process needs 4800 MJ of heat, the fuel burned has a calorific value of 44 MJ/kg and the furnace efficiency is 70 percent. Calculate the mass of fuel required in kg.
items.s: Useful heat per kg = 44 x 70/100 = 30.8 MJ, so fuel = 4800/30.8 = 155.8 kg.
items.t: Process energy, steam and heat transfer

items.q: A sample of paddy has a mass of 158 g before drying and 124 g after oven drying. Calculate its moisture content on the wet basis in percent.
items.s: Wet basis moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/wet mass x 100 = (158 - 124)/158 x 100 = 21.52 percent.

items.q: A grain sample weighs 363 g when taken and 126 g after all its moisture has been driven off. Calculate its moisture content on the dry basis in percent.
items.s: Dry basis moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/dry mass x 100 = (363 - 126)/126 x 100 = 188.1 percent.

items.q: A crop has a moisture content of 18 percent on the wet basis. Calculate the same moisture on the dry basis in percent.
items.s: Dry basis = wet basis/(100 - wet basis) x 100 = 18/(100 - 18) x 100 = 21.95 percent.

items.q: A heap of grain has a bulk density of 680 kg/m3 while the true density of the kernels is 1250 kg/m3. Calculate the porosity of the bulk in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/true density) x 100 = (1 - 680/1250) x 100 = 45.6 percent.

items.q: A silo compartment holds 2.5 m3 of grain whose bulk density is 650 kg/m3. Calculate the mass of grain stored in tonnes.
items.s: Mass = bulk density x volume = 650 x 2.5 = 1625 kg = 1.62 tonnes.

items.q: A grain particle released into still air falls 0.5 m at a steady speed in 0.6 s. Calculate its terminal velocity in m/s.
items.s: Terminal velocity = distance/time = 0.5/0.6 = 0.833 m/s.

items.q: A store must hold 900 kg of grain whose bulk density is 700 kg/m3. Calculate the volume of storage space needed in m3.
items.s: Volume = mass/bulk density = 900/700 = 1.29 m3.

items.q: A lot of 1000 kg of grain has a moisture content of 20 percent on the wet basis. Calculate the mass of water it contains in kg.
items.s: Mass of water = total mass x moisture/100 = 1000 x 20/100 = 200 kg.

items.q: A cleaner receives 250 kg of produce containing 30 kg of foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the percentage of foreign matter in the feed.
items.s: Foreign matter = 30/250 x 100 = 12 percent of the feed.

items.q: A cleaner is fed 900 kg of paddy that contains 10 percent foreign matter and removes all of it. Calculate the mass of cleaned paddy obtained in kg.
items.s: Clean paddy = feed x (100 - foreign matter)/100 = 900 x 90/100 = 810 kg.

items.q: Of 50 kg of material small enough to pass a screen, only 45 kg actually passes. Calculate the screen efficiency in percent.
items.s: Screen efficiency = mass passed/mass that should pass x 100 = 45/50 x 100 = 90 percent.

the heat needed to raise the temperature of unit mass of a substance by one degree

the mass of oil recovered from a stated mass of seed
the treatment of crude oil to remove gums, free fatty acids and colouring matter

items.q: by product may be defined as

an expense of the plant that does not change with the quantity processed
the mass of product obtained from a stated mass of raw material
the total cost of a process divided by the mass of product turned out

items.q: In this course, free fatty acid refers to
o: the mass of oil recovered from a stated mass of seed
a screw press that squeezes oil from seed and pushes out a pressed cake
an acid formed when a fat splits, used as a measure of the quality of an oil
the pressing of oil out of prepared seed by mechanical force
items.s: free fatty acid: an acid formed when a fat splits, used as a measure of the quality of an oil. The other options describe oil yield, expression, expeller.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains expeller.
o: the mass of oil recovered from a stated mass of seed
the pressing of oil out of prepared seed by mechanical force
a screw press that squeezes oil from seed and pushes out a pressed cake
the treatment of crude oil to remove gums, free fatty acids and colouring matter

items.q: “the stage of drying in which the surface begins to dry and the rate of evaporation slows” is the definition of

equilibrium moisture content
deep bed drying
constant rate period

items.q: “the separation of chaff from grain by a stream of air” is the definition of
o: screen efficiency
broken grain
winnowing
magnetic separator

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains moisture content dry basis.
o: the mass of a material divided by the volume of its solid matter alone, with all pores excluded
the mass of water in a material expressed as a percentage of the mass of its dry matter
a measure of how closely the shape of a particle approaches a sphere
the mass of a loose granular material divided by the volume it occupies when poured into a container
items.s: moisture content dry basis: the mass of water in a material expressed as a percentage of the mass of its dry matter. The other options describe true density, bulk density, sphericity.

items.q: “the drying of a sample shallow enough that the air conditions are the same throughout it” is the definition of
o: falling rate period

bound moisture
thin layer drying

items.q: Which statement correctly defines sensible heat?

the heat needed to turn unit mass of water into vapour at the same temperature
the property that fixes the rate at which heat passes through unit thickness of a material for a stated temperature difference
material of low thermal conductivity wrapped round a vessel to slow the loss of heat

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains sieving.

the separation of particles by passing them through openings of a chosen size
kernels that have been cracked or split during handling or processing
the lifting away of light impurities from a falling stream of produce by suction
items.s: sieving: the separation of particles by passing them through openings of a chosen size. The other options describe specific gravity separation, broken grain, aspiration.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines foreign matter?

the share of the material that should pass a screen which actually does pass it
the separation of chaff from grain by a stream of air
material present in a produce lot other than the produce itself
items.s: foreign matter: material present in a produce lot other than the produce itself. The other options describe screen efficiency, winnowing, specific gravity separation.

items.q: The correct meaning of aspiration is
o: the sorting of particles by the density difference between them
the lifting away of light impurities from a falling stream of produce by suction
the sorting of produce into lots of uniform size, shape or quality
the share of the material that should pass a screen which actually does pass it
items.s: aspiration: the lifting away of light impurities from a falling stream of produce by suction. The other options describe grading, specific gravity separation, screen efficiency.

items.q: In this course, respiration refers to
o: the killing of insects in stored produce by exposing them to a poisonous gas
a tall cylindrical structure for holding grain in bulk
the fall in quantity or quality of produce that takes place while it is held in store
the breathing of living produce that uses up oxygen and releases heat and moisture
items.s: respiration: the breathing of living produce that uses up oxygen and releases heat and moisture. The other options describe silo, storage losses, fumigation.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the total cost of a process divided by the mass of product turned out”

capacity utilisation
unit processing cost
extraction rate

the heat liberated when unit mass of a fuel is completely burned
material of low thermal conductivity wrapped round a vessel to slow the loss of heat

a tall cylindrical structure for holding grain in bulk

aspiration
sieving

fixed cost
material balance

the stage of drying in which the surface begins to dry and the rate of evaporation slows
the removal of moisture from a material by evaporation
the drying of a sample shallow enough that the air conditions are the same throughout it

items.q: The correct meaning of conveyor capacity is

a conveyor in which an endless moving band carries the material
a conveyor in which cups fixed to a vertical belt or chain lift material upward
the mass or volume of material a conveyor moves in unit time

items.q: Which statement correctly defines oil yield?

an acid formed when a fat splits, used as a measure of the quality of an oil
the mass of oil recovered from a stated mass of seed
the proportion of oil held in a seed on a stated basis
